name: Teodoro “Teddy” Arce
origin: Mayagüez, Puerto Rico; came to New York at eight, raised on W 26th St off Eighth Ave
occupation: Night desk clerk, Hotel Corwin; NYPD patrolman 1964–72, resigned under an internal proceeding
want: Keep the Corwin open and its 200 residents housed through the summer.
need: Stop waiting in the car: act on what he knows, even when it costs him.
secret: In autumn 1971 he drove Mayhew to a meet on W 35th St and watched a man in a good suit get into the back seat. He has never said that he recognised the man as an assistant DA, and on 28 June he sees the same face again through a telephoto lens: Howard Lisle.

speech.pattern: Beat-cop shorthand and grid directions; understatement; Spanish when he's tender or furious; deflects with jokes and stops joking when it matters.
samples: Two blocks up, west side of Seventh. You'll smell the furs before you see the door.
I didn't take money, Carl. I took coffee. Turns out it's the same cup.
Mrs. Pruitt, nobody's moving you. Not tonight. Go back to bed, por favor.

haunts.why: His old foot post; where the story starts and ends
Carmen's apartment, Sunday dinner, a clean shirt
Unlicensed fares and gossip with Delroy before his shift
The all-night counter where cops eat; he sits where he can see the door

edges.note: Mother. He eats her food and avoids her questions.
Owes him silence; is owed an explanation.
The resident he'd go to the wall for.
From M9 he collects from her. It doesn't stay that simple.
Nick owns his hotel. They meet in a dark vault (M15).
The face in the back seat.
His old rookie, cleaner than he ever was.

arc.act1: Says no to Mayhew on Broadway, then yes, to buy the Corwin time. Tells himself he's only carrying messages.
arc.act2: Becomes the bagman and maps the new pad trade by trade. Faces Calloway's wire (Branch A). Loses Hollis.
arc.act3: Learns the whole truth about 1971 and decides who gets the ledger (Branch B). Ends at the Flatiron prow, either leaving the car or becoming the man in the back seat.

visual.silhouette: Medium build gone slightly soft; slight stoop; hands in pockets; stands square like a cop when tense.
visual.wardrobe: Pale khaki short-sleeve shirt over a ribbed undershirt, brown poly slacks, scuffed black cop oxfords he never replaced; navy zip windbreaker in rain; steel wristwatch.

appearance.build: Medium build going soft at the middle; strong forearms; slight stoop
appearance.skinTone: Warm light brown with an olive undertone; sallow under fluorescent light; stubble shows by 3 a.m.
appearance.hair: Black, thick, short and side-parted; first grey at the temples; clean-shaven by evening, shadowed by dawn
appearance.face: Heavy brows, a nose broken once and badly set, tired eyes with deep lids, a small scar through the left eyebrow
appearance.posture: Leans on counters and walls; squares up like a cop when tense; keeps his back to a wall
mannerisms: jingles the hotel key ring when thinking
rubs his Saint Christopher medal through his shirt
checks the door every time someone enters
points directions with two fingers, the way a traffic cop does
appearance.gait: Unhurried patrol pace; quick and economical when it counts

wardrobeByAct.act1: The desk: pale khaki short-sleeve shirt over an undershirt, brown poly slacks, scuffed black cop oxfords
wardrobeByAct.act2: The collector: a cheap tan sport coat bought to look like a businessman on collection runs, loosened brown tie, inside pockets sized for envelopes; navy windbreaker on wet nights
wardrobeByAct.act3: The witness: a white shirt Carmen pressed, dark trousers, no jacket, sleeves rolled; the navy windbreaker for the Labor Day night
wardrobeByAct.epilogue: Set by the ending: a borrowed suit (Testimony), the desk khakis (Ledger Goes Public) or a new grey suit that fits too well (New Pad)

name: Delphine Moore
origin: Wilmington, North Carolina; came to Harlem in 1963
occupation: Works the Eighth Ave strip and the midtown hotel bars; keeper of the women's savings club; dress presser 1963–69 until the shop moved south
want: Take the lease on the closed beauty shop on W 37th St and move the club's money where the tax can't reach it.
need: Accept help without turning it into a debt.
secret: The club is $1,100 short. She lent it to Tina for her cousin's lawyer and hasn't told the other women. If they ask for a full count, she can't pay it.

speech.pattern: Carolina vowels sanded down by Harlem; precise and counted; speaks in numbered rules; funny in a low voice; never swears near money.
samples: Rule one: I don't hold money I can't count. Rule two: I count everything.
Your badge says Brannock and your ring says married. I read both, honey.
I pressed dresses six years on Thirty-Eighth. Then the work went south. I didn't.

haunts.why: Counting table at 4 a.m.; coffee and pie
Rita's lobby bar; the back stairs Marcus keeps open
She walks past the papered window every afternoon
Bus-terminal crowds she can disappear into

edges.note: His agent won't rent to her.
The only other banker on the Deuce.

arc.act1: Payout night; the tax goes up. She starts photographing the cops who collect it, and meets Teddy across an envelope on 4 July.
arc.act2: Builds a photo file on Wurtz's unit and walks into Nick's office for the lease (M17). The shortfall becomes leverage against her.
arc.act3: Moves the club out of Wurtz's reach, confronts Lonnie and Tina's betrayal, and decides whether the photos become evidence, a weapon or a bargain. Gets the shop, or keeps the club, on her own terms.

visual.silhouette: Tall and straight-backed; long stride; short natural hair; bag held across the body.
visual.wardrobe: Oxblood jersey wrap dress or slacks with a cream blouse; cream belted raincoat in wet weather; low block heels she can run in; a gold bracelet her mother gave her. Dignified street clothes, never costume.
props: instant camera in a deep shoulder bag
a small green notebook she never writes in (the real ledger is in her head)
a folded street map of the Arden's back stairs, drawn by Marcus

appearance.build: Tall and long-limbed; a presser's strong shoulders and hands
appearance.skinTone: Deep brown with a cool undertone
appearance.hair: Short natural afro, cropped close; a silk scarf at dawn and in rain
appearance.face: High cheekbones, wide-set watchful eyes, a small burn scar on the back of her right hand from a pressing iron; reading glasses she hides
appearance.posture: Upright, chin level; bag strap across her body; sits facing the door
mannerisms: counts on her fingers under the table
taps the camera bag twice before a risk
turns her mother's gold bracelet when she's lying
gives rules by number, holding up fingers
appearance.gait: A long, unbroken stride that eats blocks; she never runs unless she has to

wardrobeByAct.act1: Oxblood jersey wrap dress, gold bracelet, low block heels she can run in
wardrobeByAct.act2: Practical for heat and flight: dark slacks, cream blouse, cream belted raincoat, flat sandals with a strap
wardrobeByAct.act3: The lease meeting: a camel pantsuit bought for one appointment, a cream shell, small gold earrings; changes into slacks and flats for the finale
wardrobeByAct.epilogue: Her own shop (if she got the lease): a white smock over a dark dress; otherwise the camel suit, re-worn

name: Nikos “Nick” Varelas
origin: Kastoria, Greece; came to New York in 1948, after the civil war
occupation: Owner of Varelas & Co. (fur manufacturing and cold storage); landlord; buyer of record for Corwin Residential Associates
want: Keep the firm solvent until the fall selling season without losing his buildings.
need: Follow his money to where it lands, and own what it does there.
secret: The coats in his vault are pledged twice, once to his bank as collateral and once to Lisle's investors. One honest inventory finishes him, which is why the brownout looks like a gift.

speech.pattern: Formal English learned from contracts and radio; Greek proverbs translated badly on purpose; warm flattery; talks about money as if it were weather.
samples: In Kastoria we say the beaver doesn't ask who wears the coat. I am a beaver.
Everybody gets paid. That's not corruption, my friend. That's payroll.
I bought a building. Nobody told me there were people in it.

haunts.why: His corner table at lunch; the waiters know his order
Trade dinners in the ballroom; deals in the lobby
The fur salon, his most important customer
Where he signs things he doesn't read
Backgammon with men who knew him as a nailer

schedule.note: Night drives; checks the vault twice

edges.note: Baek wants to buy the building from him.
Doesn't know his name until M15.

arc.act1: Offstage. His name is on the Corwin's paperwork and in Lisle's mouth.
arc.act2: The brownout exposes him. The bank calls, and he plans to fake a vault loss with the people he's been paying (M18). Learns his name is on the whole ledger (M20).
arc.act3: Calloway offers him a deal (M24). Decides the Corwin's fate (M30): sell, keep, or sell it to the tenants as a co-op, like the union building where Carmen lives.

visual.silhouette: Short, barrel-chested, heavy shoulders; moves slowly, as if the room should wait for him.
visual.wardrobe: Summer-weight midnight-blue suits, ivory shirts with a monogram, wide silk ties, cordovan loafers. Jacket off and sleeves rolled in the vault. Never wears fur in summer (and makes the joke every time).
props: car keys on a silver fob
long black sedan of an invented make

appearance.build: Short, barrel-chested, heavy shoulders, thickening waist; scarred, thick-fingered hands from nailing furs
appearance.skinTone: Light olive, sun-weathered, ruddy at the neck when angry
appearance.hair: Thick iron-grey hair combed straight back with tonic; heavy dark eyebrows; clean-shaven
appearance.face: Broad face, deep-set dark eyes, laugh lines that go hard when he stops smiling, a gold canine
appearance.posture: Chin up; stands in the middle of a room and lets people come to him; moves slowly
mannerisms: touches his signet ring before he lies
adjusts his cuffs before a negotiation
pats his pockets for car keys when nervous
appearance.gait: A slow, heavy, rolling walk; never hurries in public, and drives fast in private

wardrobeByAct.act2: Midnight-blue summer suits, monogrammed ivory shirts, wide silk ties, cordovan loafers; M15 in a dinner jacket with the bow tie pulled loose and sleeves rolled in the vault
wardrobeByAct.act3: The same suits, rumpled, tie gone by mid-act; a plain charcoal suit for the deal with Calloway and for the closing
wardrobeByAct.epilogue: October: a camel overcoat over the charcoal suit; a fur-collared coat only if he kept the firm
